notes:
**The Print button shows the run.** While a job prints, the button stays lit and counts up — "Printing 12 / 150" — and reads "Waiting" when the printer is ready but no pieces are arriving. Stop is now **Finish & Stop** and says what it is doing: it prints the pieces already in the printer, then stops the machine. **Abort now** stops at once and flushes them. The Print tab shows the count from any page, and the buttons are ready again the moment the run ends, before you close the run summary.

**The printer follows the resolution you pick.** Changing the resolution on the Print page sets the printer straight away, so the belt-speed gauge and its limit match what is selected even before you print. If something else has moved the printer to another resolution, the gauge says so.

**Sensor mask for windows and flaps.** A new job setting — Job panel ▸ Media ▸ Sensor mask — makes the print sensor ignore the rest of the piece once it has triggered, so a window edge, a flap or a crease cannot fire a second print. Automatic suits most pieces; it can be adjusted, set to a fixed length, or turned off.

**Manual purge from the File menu.** File ▸ Manual Purge… opens the purge window without going through head alignment, with the job's ink profile and resolution already chosen, a tick to run the machine for the piece, and the belt-speed gauge.

**Easier to read on the canvas.** Warnings on objects — "wider than its box", a barcode that cannot be made — are large enough to read at any zoom and screen scale. Each head's name and bridge-ruler reading sit beside the piece instead of over your print, and a head dragged off the piece keeps its handle so you can pull it back. Purge bars no longer raise coverage or quiet-zone warnings. A new barcode starts empty instead of assuming an IMb field.

**Head alignment.** Scan the target from inside the window: pick your flatbed scanner, or a folder it saves into, and press Scan at the resolution you choose; light scans are now read correctly. The target keeps a margin you set clear of the leading and trailing edges, and a Stock dropdown sets the piece length. The print trigger (rising or falling edge) and the print orientation can be set here and are kept in head-stitching backups. Results are stricter and clearer: fixed tolerances, no averaging across a change, a seam inside a head corrected on the pen that closes it, and the seam between two heads reported as a head move — in ruler steps on a machine with a bridge ruler — instead of a failure. A piece that slipped between the heads is recognised and left out.

**Machine setup.** Settings ▸ Machine has a Machine model picker. The media-size list and, during installation, the machine list and ink profiles come from TNR's current lists, with the built-in copies used when the PC is offline. The installer's Detect printer matches the machine model again, a fresh install no longer shows the model as "not set", and bridge-ruler corrections save again.

**Machine control.** The printer connects as soon as it is switched on, instead of up to 15 seconds later. The link to the machine controller is steadier: connecting no longer restarts the controller, and installing an update no longer leaves it needing a power cycle. On machines whose feeder is paused by a relay, the start and stop sequences pause and release the feeder, the Print page's relay button stays in step with them, and the feeder no longer chatters while the machine starts or stops. Help ▸ Diagnostics ▸ Machine has an Expert mode for dealers: the controller's console, reset and firmware update.

**Also.** Save As shows just the job's name and opens in the job's own folder. Double-clicking a folder path on the Home tab opens that folder. The sample job has 150 records and more fields.
